concepts.def: Seljuk Turks crushed the Byzantine army and captured Emperor Romanos IV, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement and prompting later appeals to the West.
Pope Urban II's sermon calling Western knights to aid Byzantium and recover Jerusalem, launching the First Crusade with the cry 'God wills it'.
The First Crusade's bloody conquest of the holy city from its Muslim rulers, establishing Latin Christian control after a successful siege.
Latin principalities founded in the East after 1099, including the Kingdom of Jerusalem and County of Edessa, collectively called Outremer.

The Fourth Crusade, diverted from Egypt, captured and looted the Christian Byzantine capital, fatally weakening the empire it had set out to aid.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Age of the Crusades c1071-1204 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Age of the Crusades c1071-1204 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Age of the Crusades c1071-1204.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose 1095 sermon at Clermont launched the First Crusade?
options: Pope Urban II
Pope Gregory VII
Emperor Alexios I
Saladin

mcqs.q: In which 1071 battle did the Seljuks defeat the Byzantines?
options: Manzikert
Hattin
Antioch
Hastings

mcqs.q: Which leader recaptured Jerusalem after the Battle of Hattin in 1187?
options: Saladin
Richard I
Godfrey of Bouillon
Baldwin I

mcqs.q: What unexpected target did the Fourth Crusade sack in 1204?
options: Constantinople
Jerusalem
Cairo
Damascus

mcqs.q: Why did Pope Urban II call the First Crusade in 1095?
options: The Fourth Crusade conquered Egypt.
Urban II called it to conquer France.
He responded to a Byzantine appeal for military aid against the Seljuk Turks and framed the campaign as recovering the Holy Land for Christendom.
The Crusade was launched to convert all Muslims to Christianity by force.

mcqs.q: What did the Fourth Crusade actually achieve in 1204?
options: It sacked Constantinople, a Christian city, never reaching the Holy Land, severely damaging Byzantium rather than fighting Muslim powers.
The Fourth Crusade recaptured Jerusalem for the Christians.
The Fourth Crusade conquered Egypt.
Urban II called it to conquer France.

mcqs.q: Were the Crusader States permanent conquests?
options: The Crusader States covered all of the Middle East.
Once captured, Jerusalem stayed in Christian hands for centuries.
They were fragile and gradually lost, with Jerusalem falling to Saladin in 1187, despite repeated later crusades to defend Outremer.
The Fourth Crusade conquered Egypt.
